title: Inflammation-related proteins as biomarkers of treatment-related behavioral symptoms: A longitudinal study of breast cancer patients and age-matched controls
notes: Longitudinal cohort with matched controls; 4 timepoints: baseline (pre-any treatment), 1-month post-treatment, 1-year, 2-year. Joint longitudinal models with fold-change estimates. Treatment (all types including surgery-only) caused transient increases in sTNF-RII and IL-6 at 1-month post-treatment, returning to baseline by 1 year. sTNF-RII increase → worse Physical Functioning (fold-change 0.79, 95%CI 0.73-0.85 per unit ln(sTNF-RII) in patients) and worse Pain. IL-6 → worse Physical Functioning (fold-change 0.96, 95%CI 0.94-0.98, both patients and controls). IL-1RA → worse Physical Functioning (fold-change 0.93, 95%CI 0.90-0.97 in patients). CRITICALLY: NO significant associations between inflammatory markers and cognitive outcomes (Attention/Concentration unchanged, Perceived Cognitive Problems unchanged from baseline in patients). Controls showed modest improvement in cognitive measures (practice effect). Fold-change format not convertible to Cohen's d without additional distributional information. SF-36 Physical Functioning as outcome.
extraction_status: META_ONLY — no inflammation→cognition edge evidence; sTNF-RII/IL-6/IL-1RA → Physical Functioning/Pain only; cognitive outcomes (Attention/Concentration, Perceived Cognitive Problems) NULL; fold-change format not directly convertible to cohens_d
null_findings: sTNF-RII → Perceived Cognitive Problems: not significant
IL-6 → Perceived Cognitive Problems: not significant
CRP → any behavioral symptom: not significant
All inflammatory markers returned to baseline by 1-year post-treatment
